overall: Atlanta is sitting at 77.0°F at 2:50 AM with a very high dewpoint of 73.4°F (surface relative humidity near 92%) and broken clouds with a low ceiling around 427m. Temperature has been completely flat at 77°F since midnight, indicating persistent cloud cover and deep low-level moisture are preventing any radiational cooling — but also suggesting the atmosphere is laden with moisture that could limit or accelerate afternoon convective heating depending on cloud evolution.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show notable spread: NBM is most conservative at 80.8°F, ECMWF at 83.7°F, and HRRR most aggressive at 86.2°F. The META model (most reliable fusion) peaks at 86-87°F (26.4%), but the high-confidence Tier 1 ensemble odd-bucket signal strongly singles out 81-82°F at 31.8% with a 26.6% gap — a sharp disagreement that likely reflects the suppressive potential of the current dense low cloud deck and near-saturated low-level moisture.
max_temp_prediction: The deep moisture and low ceiling present at 3 AM are significant suppressors of daytime heating, favoring the NBM's more conservative 80.8°F over the HRRR's 86.2°F. Peak timing is expected around 14-15h ET, giving clouds ample time to mix out — but the extremely high dewpoints limit the potential temperature rise through evaporative and moisture effects. Weighing the META model center near 86-87°F against the Tier 1 ensemble signal at 81-82°F and the current cloudy, saturated overnight profile, a best estimate of around 84°F seems appropriate, with moderate-to-low confidence given meaningful uncertainty in how quickly (or whether) the cloud layer breaks.
